newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says keeping close watch on forex movements.
newsitem.headline: MOF says keeping close watch on forex movements.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, commenting on the dollar's rise above 117 yen, said on Thursday his ministry is keeping close watch on currency movements.
He told reporters: "We are keeping close watch on currency movements with deep interest."

Mitsuzuka said early passage of a supplementary budget for the current fiscal year and the main state budget for fiscal 1997/98, starting on April 1, was expected to have a favourable effect on the Japanese economy.
A parliament session that opens on January 20 is to consider the budgets.
Japanes economic fundamentals were improving steadily, although gradually, Mitsuzuka said.
"I am sure the markets will reflect economic fundamentals if (they realise that) the base of the Japanese economy is firm," he said.
A senior Finance Ministry official told Reuters earlier that the basic stance of the ministry on exchange rates was what Mitsuzuka had said recently.
Mitsuzuka has said that an excessively weak or strong yen is not favourable for the Japanese economy.
